topic: The Essence of Calculus: The Art of Change and Accumulation
target_audience: High school students and curious beginners

sections.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
lecture_lines: Algebra handles static shapes and constant speeds perfectly.
But the real world is curvy and constantly changing.
Calculus measures change at a specific, exact moment.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation
lecture_lines: Complex shapes are hard to measure directly.
We can approximate them using many simpler pieces.
As pieces become infinitely small, the approximation becomes exact.
animations: Show a circle (#00FFFF) with a triangle (#FFFF00) inside it. Change lecture line 1 color to #FFFF00.

As sides increase, polygon color blends into the circle color. Label: 'n -> Infinity'. Change lecture line 3 color to #FFFF00.

sections.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
lecture_lines: Zooming into any smooth curve eventually reveals a line.
This straight line represents the instantaneous rate of change.
On a roller coaster, your direction is a tangent.
We find this by narrowing the gap between points.
This process of finding slopes is called differentiation.

sections.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
lecture_lines: Integration glues tiny, infinite pieces back into a whole.
It calculates the total accumulation over a period.
Visually, this is the area under a curve.
If we sum every tiny drip from a bucket...
We find the total volume of water lost.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are actually perfect opposites.
One finds the slope, the other finds the area.
A climber’s steepness at any point determines their height.
Tracking growth rate reveals the total growth achieved.
This bridge connects the rate of change to accumulation.

sections.title: Calculus in Action: The Modern World
lecture_lines: Calculus is the engine powering modern physics and engineering.
It guides planets in orbit and rockets landing safely.
We use it to model anything that moves or changes.
